task.question: What breakthrough did physicists at Northwestern University demonstrate on October 21?
task.evidence: 21 October – Physicists at Northwestern University demonstrate the first one-positron quantum cyclotron, trapping a single positron (the antimatter counterpart of the electron) for months and controlling its quantum states. The breakthrough could enable unprecedented measurements of the particle's magnetic moment, providing more stringent tests of CPT symmetry.

answer: On October 21, 2026, physicists at Northwestern University demonstrated the first one-positron quantum cyclotron, trapping a single positron for months. FINAL: Trapped single positron for months.

3 October – Researchers at the University of Bonn report converting human blood cells into neural stem cells with substantially reduced epigenetic ages. Cells from an 80-year-old donor exhibited a molecular age of less than 20 years, with most age-related epigenetic changes reversing over approximately 50 days. The findings could help scientists investigate the mechanisms of cellular reprogramming
